steps.title: TOOL DECODING: A PLUG-AND-PLAY APPROACH TO ENHANCING LANGUAGE MODELS FOR TOOL USAGE

conclusion: The paper’s central contribution is the “Tool Decoding” mechanism, a training‑free, plug‑and‑play decoding procedure that injects tool signatures into constrained decoding to improve tool selection and tool calls. However, very closely related work already delivers this core idea: TOOLDEC (“Don't Fine-Tune, Decode: Syntax Error-Free Tool Use via Constrained Decoding”) proposes a model-agnostic, training-free constrained decoding method that derives syntactic constraints from tool documentation and masks invalid tokens to enforce valid tool names and argument formats, directly targeting tool use at inference time. Similarly, Wang et al. (2024) (“FANTAstic SEquences”) and Wang et al. (2023) implement training-free, API-aware constrained decoding using signatures/regex and trie or DP-based token restriction, again to ensure valid function and argument generation and to substantially improve tool-use performance on API-Bank. Relative to this body of work, the submission mainly adds an “order consistency” heuristic that aggregates multiple sampled parameter orders to reduce value errors, some taxonomy refinements, and additional experiments over more models/benchmarks. These deltas are secondary design details and expanded evaluation rather than a new core mechanism. Given that the central idea—tool-specific, training-free constrained decoding for tool use—is already well established, the overall novelty is not strong enough for a top-tier venue.

core_judgments: The novelty of the approach is limited, as constrained decoding for tool usage in LLMs has already been explored in several prior works, including Domino and TOOLDEC.
The specific implementation of constrained decoding in this paper does not differ significantly from these existing methods.
The primary novel contribution lies in the introduction of the order consistency mechanism, but this addition offers only a limited improvement, as evidenced by the results in Table 6.
